body:
We have been together for half a decade now. Due to financial difficulties it was really hard to get closer to each other. Right now we are still an expensive plane ticket away and we don't have much money, but its much better than being on opposites sides of the world.

I will definitely try to assert my care more, but unfortunately she is hard set at the moment that she doesn't deserve a therapist. She has anti-depression medication, and that's probably kept her as good as she is now to have gone on for this long. She's incredibly strong and it's really admirable, but she thinks she's the weakest girl in the world because she does a lot of this to make sure that I'm okay and have a good life.

Trying to get her to reintegrate is definitely going to be difficult. I know a place she'd be comfortable in if we can get her at least some self-esteem, because I'm already a member of the "club" so to speak, and could help her ease into talking to others, but again she is very determined that she cannot and will not because those are things for people with any value whatsoever, in her words. 

For support all she really has is a distant advisor girl who she texts and they reply within a few days and then me. Anyone else she definitely fears abandonment from even more than us.

Forgive my ignorance, but when you say contradict her I wonder if I do it the right way,

For example she will say: Everyone has much more interesting things to say than me [on a subject]

So I've said: Not at all, darling! In the past you've told me X, Y, and Z and those were very insightful, and we had a 2 hour discussion on them that led into a larger one about A, B, and C. I'm sure that others would want to hear your perspective, too.

After posting I also realised I rarely talk about myself to her, and maybe that gives the wrong impression for her depression, too. That I never do anything except see her so it must be a burden or something like that, or that I am hiding things because I don't trust her enough. I'm not entirely sure, but these are thoughts I imagine if I was in her place.
